The drawing shows a thiophene ring with sulfur at the bottom. A nitro group (O2N) is attached to the ring carbon on the left, next to S. A nitrile group (C≡N) is attached to the ring carbon at the top right.

Numbering the ring from S as position 1:
- C2 is the lower-left carbon, bearing the nitro group. In the usual numbering this is the "5" position.
- C3 is the upper-left carbon, a CH.
- C4 is the upper-right carbon, bearing the nitrile. This is the "3" position.
- C5 is the lower-right carbon, a CH next to S.

So the molecule is 5-nitrothiophene-3-carbonitrile.

Ring bonds: the double bond between the nitro-bearing carbon and the adjacent CH (upper-left), and the double bond between the nitrile-bearing carbon and the CH next to S (lower-right).

SMILES: N#Cc1csc([N+](=O)[O-])c1

Atom-by-atom check: c1 (the nitrile-bearing carbon), c (CH), s, c (the nitro-bearing carbon), then c1 (the CH between the nitro-bearing and nitrile-bearing carbons). The ring has 5 atoms, and the connectivity matches the drawing.

SMILES: N#Cc1csc([N+](=O)[O-])c1
